\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient of an affine combination]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeff_affineCombination}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeff_affineCombination}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\theta\in\mathbb R$, let
$f,g:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. For
$h:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, write $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E_x[h(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i]$,
where the expectation is uniform over the Boolean cube. Then $\widehat{\theta
f+(1-\theta)g}(S)=\theta\widehat f(S)+(1-\theta)\widehat g(S)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Fourier square functional]
\lean{FABL.fourierSquareFunctional}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p065-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p211-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p211-b005
}
\label{FABL.fourierSquareFunctional}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff}
For a real-valued function $f$ on $\{-1,1\}^n$ and a real weight $c(S)$ for every subset
$S$ of the coordinate indices, define the Fourier square functional by
$\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}c(S)\widehat f(S)^2$, where $\widehat f(S)$ is the
Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$.
\end{definition}

  {FABL.fourierSquareFunctional}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p065-b001}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $c(S)\ge 0$ be a real weight for each subset
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$. For any real-valued functions $f,g$ on the sign cube and any
$\theta\in[0,1]$, the weighted sum of squared Fourier coefficients of $\theta
f+(1-\theta)g$ is at most $\theta$ times that of $f$ plus $1-\theta$ times that of $g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Convexity of the Fourier square functional]
\lean{FABL.convexOn_fourierSquareFunctional}
\label{FABL.convexOn_fourierSquareFunctional}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierSquareFunctional, FABL.fourierSquareFunctional_affine_le}
\difficulty{3}
For a natural number $n$, let $c$ assign a real number $c(S)$ to each subset $S$ of
$\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and suppose $c(S)\ge 0$ for every $S$. On the space of real-valued
functions on $\{-1,1\}^n$, the functional that sends $f$ to $\sum_S c(S)\widehat
f(S)^2$, where $\widehat f(S)$ is the uniform average of $f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, is
convex.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier square functional of an average]
\lean{FABL.fourierSquareFunctional_uniformExpectation_le}
\label{FABL.fourierSquareFunctional_uniformExpectation_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.convexOn_fourierSquareFunctional, FABL.fourierSquareFunctional}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $c(S)\ge 0$ for every subset
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\{f_i\}_{i\in I}$ be a nonempty finite family of
real-valued functions on the sign cube. The weighted sum of squared Fourier coefficients
of the pointwise uniform average $|I|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I} f_i$ is at most the uniform
average of the corresponding weighted sums for the individual functions.
\end{theorem}
